references_named: Mladen Stilinović, An Artist Who Cannot Speak English Is No Artist (1992)
rationale: The work cleanly restages Stilinović's 1992 banner as a live browser gate that actually executes the test the original only implied. The mechanism (navigator.languages string check) is the argument: art-world legitimacy reduced to a locale tag, gameable by editing a preference. It reads at two depths (dry gag vs. critique of English hegemony), holds the ethics floor (no network, no storage, CC BY-SA, attribution visible regardless of verdict), and is materially distinct from the catalogue — no prior work uses navigator.languages as the gate. The aside lines land the double-coding without requiring wall text. Restraint is exemplary: one sentence, one check, one ruling.
reservations: The 'artist' verdict's aside ('No further proof was required. A certificate is not available. There is nothing to frame.') is slightly more elegant than the 'no artist' aside, which leans a touch explanatory; the asymmetry is minor but worth noting. Novelty is high but not maximal — the navigator.languages-as-material move is a recognizable net.art gesture, even if not previously catalogued here.
revision_suggestion: Consider tightening the 'no artist' aside so both branches land with equal restraint, e.g. matching the brevity of the 'artist' branch and letting the appeal instruction sit as a separate, smaller line rather than embedded in the aside paragraph.
